title: Geography Collection: Land, Borders, and Islands
description: Three curated 15-question geography sets covering physical geography, political boundaries, and islands and seas.

questions.prompt: Which river runs through the Grand Canyon?
questions.hint: The river shares its name with a U.S. state upstream.
questions.explanation: The Colorado River carved and continues to flow through the Grand Canyon.

questions.prompt: The Andes run mainly along which side of South America?
questions.hint: The range parallels the continent's Pacific coast.
questions.explanation: The Andes extend along the western edge of South America.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between southern Europe and northern Africa?
questions.hint: Its name can be translated as 'in the middle of the land.'
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean Sea separates southern Europe from northern Africa.

questions.prompt: Quito, the capital of Ecuador, lies in which mountain system?
questions.hint: This range follows western South America.
questions.explanation: Quito stands in an Andean valley at high elevation.

questions.prompt: The Danube River ultimately empties into which sea?
questions.hint: Its delta lies mainly in Romania and Ukraine.
questions.explanation: The Danube reaches the Black Sea through the Danube Delta.

questions.prompt: The Great Dividing Range extends along the eastern side of which country?
questions.hint: The range divides coastal drainage from inland drainage.
questions.explanation: The Great Dividing Range forms an extensive highland system in eastern Australia.

questions.prompt: Which two rivers meet to form the Río de la Plata estuary?
questions.hint: One river shares its name with a country on the estuary's northern shore.
questions.explanation: The Paraná and Uruguay rivers converge at the head of the Río de la Plata.

questions.prompt: Lake Tana is the principal source of which major river?
questions.hint: The river joins another branch of the Nile at Khartoum.
questions.explanation: The Blue Nile flows from Lake Tana in the Ethiopian Highlands.

questions.prompt: Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat, is in which country?
questions.hint: It occupies part of the high Altiplano.
questions.explanation: Salar de Uyuni lies in southwestern Bolivia.

questions.prompt: Challenger Deep, Earth's deepest known seabed point, lies in which trench?
questions.hint: The trench is in the western Pacific near Guam.
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep is the deepest surveyed part of the Mariana Trench.

questions.prompt: Angel Falls descends from which type of flat-topped landform?
questions.hint: The waterfall begins high above Venezuela's Guiana Highlands.
questions.explanation: Angel Falls drops from the edge of Auyán-tepui, a table-top mountain in Venezuela.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range separates the Tarim Basin from the Tibetan Plateau?
questions.hint: The range forms much of the plateau's northern rim.
questions.explanation: The Kunlun Mountains separate the Tarim Basin to the north from the Tibetan Plateau to the south.

questions.prompt: What term describes a drainage basin with no outlet to the ocean?
questions.hint: Water in such a basin terminates inland through evaporation or infiltration.
questions.explanation: An endorheic basin retains drainage internally rather than discharging to an ocean.

questions.prompt: At the Afar Triple Junction, the East African Rift meets which two spreading systems?

choices.text: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden rifts

questions.hint: Both systems are associated with waters bordering the Horn of Africa.
questions.explanation: The Afar Triple Junction joins the East African, Red Sea, and Gulf of Aden rift systems.

questions.prompt: Water from Triple Divide Peak in Montana can ultimately reach which three bodies of water?

choices.text: Pacific Ocean, Arctic Ocean, and Great Salt Lake
Atlantic Ocean, Lake Superior, and Gulf of California
Hudson Bay, Arctic Ocean, and Gulf of California
Pacific Ocean, Gulf of Mexico, and Hudson Bay

questions.hint: Its three drainage routes use the Columbia, Mississippi–Missouri, and Saskatchewan systems.
questions.explanation: Drainage from Triple Divide Peak reaches the Pacific, the Gulf of Mexico, and Hudson Bay.

questions.prompt: Which two countries share the world's longest international land border?
questions.hint: The border includes a long section along the 49th parallel.
questions.explanation: Canada and the United States share the world's longest international land boundary.

questions.prompt: Which language is the official language of Brazil?
questions.hint: Brazil was colonized by a different Iberian power from most of its neighbors.
questions.explanation: Portuguese is Brazil's official language.

questions.prompt: The Isthmus of Panama connects North America with which continent?
questions.hint: The isthmus forms Central America's southern end.
questions.explanation: The Isthmus of Panama is the land bridge between North and South America.

questions.prompt: Apart from its Atlantic coast, The Gambia is almost entirely surrounded by which country?
questions.hint: The neighboring country lies both north and south of The Gambia.
questions.explanation: Senegal surrounds The Gambia on every landward side.

questions.prompt: Ouagadougou is the capital of which country?
questions.hint: The landlocked country was formerly called Upper Volta.
questions.explanation: Ouagadougou is the capital and largest city of Burkina Faso.

questions.prompt: Kaliningrad is an exclave of which country?
questions.hint: It is separated from the rest of its country by Lithuania and Belarus.
questions.explanation: Kaliningrad Oblast is a Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea.

questions.prompt: Point Roberts, reachable by land from the rest of its country only through Canada, belongs to which country?
questions.hint: Traveling there by land requires crossing the Canadian border.
questions.explanation: Point Roberts belongs to Washington state but is connected by land only to British Columbia.

questions.prompt: The Musandam Peninsula is an exclave of which country?
questions.hint: It overlooks the Strait of Hormuz.
questions.explanation: Musandam is separated from the rest of Oman by the United Arab Emirates.

questions.prompt: Baarle-Hertog consists of Belgian enclaves within which country?
questions.hint: Some of the enclaves themselves contain pieces of Baarle-Nassau.
questions.explanation: Baarle-Hertog is a Belgian municipality composed largely of enclaves in the Netherlands.

questions.prompt: The town of Llívia is a Spanish exclave surrounded by which country?
questions.hint: It lies in the Pyrenees just beyond Spain's main border.
questions.explanation: Llívia is Spanish territory surrounded by France.

questions.prompt: Campione d'Italia is an Italian enclave within which country?
questions.hint: The enclave sits beside Lake Lugano.
questions.explanation: Campione d'Italia is Italian territory enclosed by Switzerland.

questions.prompt: Sovereignty over the Vennbahn railway created several enclaves of Germany inside which country?
questions.hint: The railway territory changed hands after the First World War.
questions.explanation: Belgian sovereignty over parts of the Vennbahn left several small German enclaves west of the line.

questions.prompt: Nahwa, a counter-enclave inside Oman's Madha enclave, belongs to which country?
questions.hint: The surrounding Madha enclave lies within the same federation.
questions.explanation: Nahwa belongs to the United Arab Emirates and is enclosed by Oman's Madha enclave.

questions.prompt: Which sovereign country has territory in all four geographic hemispheres?
questions.hint: Its islands cross both the Equator and the 180th meridian.
questions.explanation: Kiribati spans north and south of the Equator and east and west of the 180th meridian.

questions.prompt: Which pair are the world's only two doubly landlocked sovereign countries?
questions.hint: Every country bordering either member of the pair is itself landlocked.
questions.explanation: Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan are each surrounded entirely by landlocked countries.

questions.prompt: Bali is an island of which country?
questions.hint: The country contains thousands of islands between Asia and Australia.
questions.explanation: Bali is one of Indonesia's best-known islands.

questions.prompt: What is the largest island in the Hawaiian archipelago?
questions.hint: It is commonly called the Big Island.
questions.explanation: Hawaiʻi, or the Big Island, is the archipelago's largest island.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates New Zealand's North and South Islands?
questions.hint: It is named for a British explorer.
questions.explanation: Cook Strait separates New Zealand's two principal islands.

questions.prompt: Madagascar lies in which ocean?
questions.hint: It lies east of Mozambique.
questions.explanation: Madagascar is an island country in the western Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which is the northernmost of Japan's four main islands?
questions.hint: Sapporo is its largest city.
questions.explanation: Hokkaido is the northernmost of Japan's four main islands.

questions.prompt: Which three countries share the island of Borneo?
questions.hint: One is a small sultanate on the island's northern coast.
questions.explanation: Borneo is divided among Brunei, Indonesia, and Malaysia.

questions.prompt: Which sea is defined by ocean currents rather than by surrounding land?
questions.hint: It is named for floating brown algae.
questions.explanation: The Sargasso Sea has no land boundary and is instead bounded by Atlantic currents.

questions.prompt: Ngerulmud is the capital of which Pacific island country?
questions.hint: The country is part of Micronesia and lies east of the Philippines.
questions.explanation: Ngerulmud, on Babeldaob island, is the capital of Palau.

questions.prompt: The Strait of Malacca lies between Sumatra and which peninsula?
questions.hint: Singapore lies near the strait's southeastern entrance.
questions.explanation: The Strait of Malacca separates Sumatra from the Malay Peninsula.

questions.prompt: The island of Socotra belongs to which country?
questions.hint: It lies east of the Horn of Africa near the Gulf of Aden.
questions.explanation: Socotra and its surrounding archipelago are part of Yemen.

questions.prompt: The autonomous Åland Islands belong to which country?
questions.hint: The islands are Swedish-speaking but politically associated with another Nordic state.
questions.explanation: Åland is an autonomous, demilitarized region of Finland.

questions.prompt: Torres Strait separates Australia from which large island?
questions.hint: The island's western half belongs to Indonesia.
questions.explanation: Torres Strait lies between Australia's Cape York Peninsula and New Guinea.

questions.prompt: The Makassar Strait separates Borneo from which island?
questions.hint: The island to the east has four long peninsulas.
questions.explanation: The Makassar Strait runs between Borneo and Sulawesi.

questions.prompt: Which three islands form the principal Mascarene Islands?
questions.hint: They lie east of Madagascar.
questions.explanation: Mauritius, Réunion, and Rodrigues are the principal islands of the Mascarene group.

questions.prompt: The Kerguelen Islands form part of which French overseas territory?
questions.hint: The territory also administers the Crozet Islands and several subantarctic districts.
questions.explanation: The Kerguelen Islands are a district of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

sets.description: Fifteen questions progressing from familiar rivers and mountain ranges to advanced landforms, tectonics, and watersheds.

sets.title: Borders and Human Geography
sets.description: Fifteen questions moving from familiar borders and languages to enclaves, counter-enclaves, and unusual territorial patterns.

sets.title: Islands, Seas, and Archipelagos
sets.description: Fifteen questions traveling from famous islands to remote straits, autonomous archipelagos, and subantarctic territories.
